predictions.title: AI-found-vuln cohort programs ship shared disclosure standard by Q1 2027
predictions.body: Anthropic's Project Glasswing first public update logged 10,000+ high- or critical-severity findings across roughly 50 maintainer partners — Mozilla closed 271 Firefox vulnerabilities at 10x its prior rate, Cloudflare surfaced 2,000 bugs of which 400 were rated high or critical, 530 disclosures were sent to maintainers with 75 patches landed, and wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 (a certificate-forgery flaw rated CVSS 9.1) was patched on a TLS library embedded in roughly five billion IoT, automotive, and industrial-control devices. The structural force is that once one frontier lab demonstrates an AI-found-vulnerability cohort program at this volume with public maintainer-side disclosure, every peer lab's responsible-scaling and preparedness narrative has to either ship an equivalent program or publicly explain why not, and every maintainer-side CI fuzzing gate has to either ingest AI-found-vuln signal as a first-class input or rebut its precision. The second-order force is that enterprise procurement teams refuse to map N vendor-specific finding-disclosure formats into N risk-acceptance frameworks, which is the same coordination pressure that converged hyperscaler RPS templates and SBOM formats. By Q1 2027 we expect at least two of OpenAI, Google DeepMind, xAI, and Mistral to ship publicly-named AI-vuln cohort programs with disclosed finding counts and maintainer-partner lists, and a standards body (most likely the Frontier Model Forum, the OpenSSF, or CISA in coordination with the EU CRA secretariat) to publish a draft AI-found-vuln disclosure-format standard covering finding provenance, false-positive accounting, and maintainer-facing reproduction-package shape. Bear case is a one-off Glasswing-cohort precision retraction that erodes the reference-point status before peer labs commit; absent that retraction, Q1 2027 lands the first AI-found-vuln cohort programs as a Tier-1 lab category and the first shared disclosure-format draft on the table.

reasoning.because: Project Glasswing logged 10,000+ AI-found findings, 530 high/critical disclosures, wolfSSL CVSS 9.1
reasoning.given: One frontier-lab AI-vuln cohort at this scale forces peer labs + maintainer CI to ingest or rebut
reasoning.so_that: At least two peer labs ship cohort programs and a standards body drafts a shared disclosure-format standard
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027; two peer-lab cohort programs plus one standards-body draft
reasoning.plain_language: Anthropic's AI found 10,000 security bugs this year. Other AI labs will copy the program and the industry will agree on shared reporting rules.

predictions.summary: Project Glasswing logged 10,000+ AI-found findings, 530 high/critical disclosures, 75 maintainer patches, plus wolfSSL CVSS 9.1 in ~5B devices. By Q1 2027 two peer frontier labs ship equivalent AI-vuln cohort programs and a standards body publishes a shared disclosure-format draft.

predictions.title: SEC publishes AI compute prebuy disclosure concept release by Q1 2027
predictions.body: By Q1 2027 the SEC Division of Corporation Finance publishes a formal concept release establishing disclosure expectations for multi-year AI compute prebuy commitments, with the rulemaking thread accelerated by the SpaceX S-1 / Musk X-post collision visible on the Thursday tape. The trigger is mechanical: SpaceX's May 20 S-1 describes Anthropic as agreeing to a $1.25 billion monthly fee through May 2029 — a ~$45 billion three-year commitment language — while Musk on X characterized the same arrangement as a 180-day lease with 90-day mutual cancellation, putting the maximum obligation at ~$7.5 billion and reserving the right to reclaim the Memphis Colossus 1 capacity for xAI if compute gets tight, leaving a roughly $37.5 billion gap between two filings that describe the same Colossus 1 asset. With SpaceX's institutional roadshow opening Monday June 8 at a $1.75T-$2T target / ~$75B raise and SPCX pricing scheduled June 11 / first trade June 12, the Division gets a real-time test case for how 'committed compute revenue' versus 'cancellable capacity lease' should be drawn inside an S-1 footnote — and an analyst pool that will spend the roadshow Q&A pressing every peer (CoreWeave, Crusoe, Lambda, Nebius, Oracle OCI AI, the still-private xAI) on the same line. Expect the concept release to specifically address three things: minimum disclosure granularity for committed compute revenue (monthly fee × term length × cancellation optionality, not lump-sum), counterparty-symmetry expectations when both sides of a deal file inside the same fiscal window, and the line between an executory contract footnote and a recognized revenue stream when the obligation runs through the IPO horizon of the counterparty. The release lands as a concept release rather than a proposed rule because the disclosure question crosses Reg S-K Item 101 / Item 303 / Item 11(h) and the staff needs comment-period input before drafting. Bear case is the release slips into Q2 2027 if the comment-period queue collides with the broader AI-revenue-recognition rulemaking already in motion; absent that slip, Q1 2027 lands the first formal SEC corp-fin disclosure document explicitly naming multi-year AI compute prebuy commitments as a distinct disclosure category.

reasoning.because: SpaceX S-1 ($45B/3yr) vs Musk X-post (180-day lease, ~$7.5B) opens a $37.5B gap on one Colossus deal
reasoning.given: SPCX prices June 11; Anthropic IPO targeted October — both counterparties file in one window
reasoning.so_that: SEC corp-fin publishes a concept release on compute prebuy granularity, counterparty symmetry, executory-vs-revenue
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027; concept release with comment period, not proposed rule
reasoning.plain_language: Two filings about the same AI compute deal disagree by $37 billion. The SEC will write new rules so this stops happening.

predictions.summary: SpaceX's S-1 describes the Anthropic Colossus 1 deal as a ~$45B three-year commitment while Musk on X calls it a 180-day cancellable lease worth ~$7.5B — a $37.5B gap as SPCX prices June 11. By Q1 2027 the SEC publishes a concept release on compute prebuy granularity and counterparty symmetry.

predictions.title: Cross-sector CERT bodies issue joint AI-found embedded-CVE guidance by Q3 2027
predictions.body: By Q3 2027 at least four sector-specific cybersecurity authorities — CISA (industrial control systems), the FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health (medical devices), NHTSA's Office of Vehicle Safety Research (automotive), and ENISA's transport-sector unit (covering the EU Cyber Resilience Act perimeter) — publish coordinated disclosure and remediation guidance explicitly naming AI-discovered vulnerabilities in shared cryptographic libraries embedded across IoT, automotive, and industrial-control device fleets, with wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 (CVSS 9.1, certificate-forgery flaw in a TLS library Anthropic's Project Glasswing surfaced inside roughly five billion devices) cited as the reference case. The cross-sectoral coordination problem is structural: a single AI-discovered cryptographic flaw lands simultaneously inside infusion pumps (FDA jurisdiction), vehicle telematics units (NHTSA), grid-edge SCADA controllers (CISA), and rail/aviation signalling (TSA / ENISA transport) — and each sectoral regulator currently runs its own disclosure cadence, its own remediation SLA, and its own software-bill-of-materials format. Project Glasswing's 10,000+ findings cohort and the 530 high/critical maintainer disclosures it has already moved through the embargo pipeline force the question: when one AI run produces a five-billion-device exposure across four sectoral regimes inside a single CVE, can a sector-by-sector response actually mitigate the cascade in time. The forcing function is mechanical — the EU Cyber Resilience Act's manufacturer obligations come into force across 2027, the FDA's pre-market and post-market cybersecurity guidance is on a 2027 refresh cycle following the 2024 final guidance, and CISA's Secure by Design pledge program will have absorbed at least two more AI-found embedded-CVE waves by the end of Q1 2027 if the Glasswing cadence holds. Expect the coordinated guidance to land via a memorandum of understanding or joint advisory between the named authorities (CISA-FDA-NHTSA-ENISA at minimum), specifying a uniform SBOM disclosure format for AI-found vulnerabilities in shared dependencies, a tiered remediation SLA keyed to device-population scale and operational-criticality, and a named coordination point of contact at the frontier lab that ran the scan. The bear case is that CISA and ENISA ship parallel but unreconciled guidance, with FDA and NHTSA each waiting for the other sector to publish first, slipping the four-way coordinated document into 2028; absent that fragmentation, Q3 2027 lands the first cross-sector coordinated guidance naming AI-discovered embedded vulnerabilities as a distinct disclosure class.

reasoning.because: wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 (CVSS 9.1) hits ~5B IoT/automotive/ICS devices across four sectoral regimes
reasoning.given: EU CRA 2027 in-force date + FDA 2027 cyber guidance refresh + CISA Secure by Design pledge
reasoning.so_that: CISA, FDA, NHTSA, ENISA publish joint disclosure-and-remediation guidance naming AI-found embedded CVEs
reasoning.landing: Q3 2027; four-authority MoU or joint advisory with uniform SBOM + tiered SLA
reasoning.plain_language: One AI scan just found a bug in software used in five billion devices, so safety agencies will write shared rules together by 2027.

predictions.summary: wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 (CVSS 9.1), the certificate-forgery flaw Project Glasswing surfaced, landed inside ~5B IoT, automotive, and industrial-control devices spanning four sectoral regimes at once. By Q3 2027 CISA, FDA, NHTSA, and ENISA publish joint guidance naming AI-found embedded CVEs.
